title: For such a time as this (Esther 4:14)
hook: "who knoweth whether thou art not come to royal estate for such a time as this?"
carry: the strange road that brought her here

segments.voice: Yesterday, the whole gate bowed to Haman, and one man stayed standing. Your line was the city of Shushan was perplexed. Where did you stay upright, even a little? Today, the news of Haman's decree reaches the palace. Day eight hundred sixty-seven.

The news reaches the queen secondhand. Her maids come and tell Esther that Mordecai is outside the king's gate in sackcloth and ashes. In every province where the decree has gone, the text says, there's mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping. Esther sends Mordecai clothes. He won't put them on. So the messages begin, carried back and forth by a servant named Hatach. Mordecai sends a copy of the decree and asks her to go to the king and plead for her people. Esther's answer is careful, and it's true. Anyone who walks into the inner court without being called is put to death, unless the king holds out his golden scepter. And she hasn't been called, she says, for thirty days. Then Mordecai sends back an answer, and it ends in a question.
screen: `SACKCLOTH OUTSIDE THE GATE.` → `MESSAGES THROUGH HATACH.` → `NOT CALLED FOR THIRTY DAYS.`

segments.voice: He starts bluntly. In the King James words: "Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king's house, more than all the Jews." The palace walls won't hide her. Then he says something stranger. If she stays silent, help will still come to the Jews, from another place. Mordecai doesn't think the rescue depends on her alone. The question is whether she'll be part of it. And then, in the 1917 Jewish translation: "who knoweth whether thou art not come to royal estate for such a time as this?" Notice it's a question. Who knows. Mordecai doesn't promise her it will work. He doesn't tell her she was born for this. He only asks her to consider that the strange road that brought her here, the orphan raised by her cousin, the girl taken into the palace, the queen who kept her people a secret, might have been leading to this one moment. The thing that kept her safe and quiet is the very thing that gives her a voice now. Some readers linger on that phrase, from another place. The book of Esther is a story where help arrives through ordinary people, timing and nerve, and some readers hear in another place a quiet hint of God. Others hear simply that the people will survive somehow. Either way, the question lands on Esther. A palace is far from a kitchen. But there may be a place where you stand, a meeting, a family table, a group chat, a classroom, where you could say a thing that needs saying.
screen: `THE PALACE WON'T HIDE HER.` · `HELP WILL COME FROM ANOTHER PLACE.` · `WHO KNOWETH: A QUESTION, NOT A PROMISE.` · then, large: `FOR SUCH A TIME AS THIS.` · then: `THE HIDDEN QUEEN, IN THE RIGHT ROOM.`

segments.voice: Today's practice is to step up for one thing. Settle, and let your breath slow down. Walk in your mind through the places you'll stand this week: a desk, a kitchen, a phone, a team, a family. Go slowly. In one of them, there may be something you're placed to say or do. Not the whole rescue. One thing. A word to the right person. A call you've been putting off. Don't decide yet. Just set Mordecai's question beside it: who knows whether you're here for this. If you pray, you can bring it to God in words from your tradition, or in silence. The bell holds the time.
Royal estate. Mordecai's question to Esther: who knows whether she came to royal estate for such a time as this. Today's word.
Your line: the strange road that brought her here. Today, do the one thing you found, or the first small piece of it, before evening. Day eight hundred sixty-seven.

original.note: Hebrew: for a time like this, from Mordecai's question in Esther 4:14.

trapdoor: what you thought: a motivational line about destiny.
what it means: a question to a queen who could stay safe: maybe this moment is why you reached the palace.
what a scholar hears: it's a question, who knoweth, and the help from another place is left unnamed. some readers hear God there.
